extension.description: Render ```wavedrom code blocks and images with embedded WaveJSON (modern theme) inside the built-in Markdown preview, and open them in a visual editor that writes the result back to the file.
command.editActive.title: WaveDrom: Edit a diagram in the current Markdown file
command.editFromPreview.title: Edit waveform
config.previewEditAffordance.menu: No visible entry point — right-click the waveform → "Edit waveform" (default)
config.previewEditAffordance.button: Show a pencil icon button at the waveform's top-right corner
config.previewEditAffordance.block: No button; clicking anywhere on the waveform opens the editor
config.previewEditAffordance.desc: How to enter the visual editor from the Markdown preview. The **right-click menu works in all three modes**; if the preview does not change, reopen it with Ctrl+Shift+V. The "Edit waveform" CodeLens in the source is controlled separately by `wavedrom-gui.showCodeLens`.
config.editorPanelPosition.current: Open as a tab in the focused editor group (default) — clicked from the preview it shares that group, adding no extra column
config.editorPanelPosition.beside: Open in a new column to the right of the editor area (VS Code's default behaviour)
config.editorPanelPosition.below: Open in a new column below the current one — from the preview this puts the preview on top and the editor underneath
config.editorPanelPosition.newWindow: Move the editor into a separate window (VS Code's "Move Editor into New Window")
config.editorPanelPosition.desc: Where the visual editor panel opens. Floating the panel **on top of** the preview is not possible: VS Code does not expose floating/modal editors to extensions (`ViewColumn` only has Active / Beside / 1-9).
config.showCodeLens.desc: Show an "Edit waveform" CodeLens above every ` ```wavedrom ` code block in the Markdown source. This entry point bypasses the preview entirely and is independent of the preview security level, so it makes a stable fallback; turn it off if you find the line noisy.
config.editorViewMode.simple: Open the editor in its simplified (mobile) layout — every time the panel is opened (default)
config.editorViewMode.auto: Do not touch the layout; use whatever the editor UI has remembered
config.editorViewMode.desc: Which layout the visual editor panel opens with. `simple` forces the compact (mobile) layout regardless of panel width, which suits the narrow editor column the panel usually gets; you can still switch layouts inside the panel (the next open returns to this setting). `auto` leaves the layout to the editor UI's own preference.
config.editorSidePanel.shown: Expand the "Lanes & groups" panel every time the editor opens (default; the editor UI itself hides it by default)
config.editorSidePanel.auto: Do not touch it; use whatever the editor UI has remembered
config.editorSidePanel.desc: Whether the editor panel opens with the "Lanes & groups" column expanded. It only takes effect in the compact (mobile) layout — see `wavedrom-gui.editorViewMode`. With `auto` the panel keeps whatever state the editor UI remembered.
config.language.auto: Follow VS Code's display language (default). If it cannot be determined, Chinese is used as the fallback
config.language.desc: Language used for the extension's messages, the "Edit waveform" CodeLens and the preview entry points. `auto` follows VS Code's display language; messages also fall back to the built-in Chinese table when VS Code's own localization pipeline returns nothing. Note that command titles and settings descriptions come from VS Code's manifest localization, which this setting cannot override.
command.openImage.title: Open with WaveDrom-Gui Editor
config.imageExportTheme.auto: Faithful to each image's own export style (default) — detected from its embedded marker or fingerprint
config.imageExportTheme.modern: Always redraw in the modern style, regardless of the image's origin
config.imageExportTheme.traditional: Always redraw in the official WaveDrom (traditional) style, regardless of the image's origin
config.imageExportTheme.desc: Pixel style used when an edited waveform image is saved. Applies when the editor panel is opened; panels already open keep their style. The embedded WaveJSON is always updated either way.
